translations.translation: With the help of Heaven.
Shabbos Parshas Vayeitzei,
the 9th of Kislev,
the eve of the 10th of Kislev,
the year 5742*

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the Mitteler Rebbe's maamar "Atah Echad," which delineates four levels of the three lines of ChaGaT throughout the entire order of Hishtalshelus, beginning from before the Tzimtzum.

translations.translation: "You are One
and Your Name is One, and who is like Your people Israel,
one nation in the land etc.,"
and it is explained by the Mitteler Rebbe, the Baal HaHilula of the 9th of Kislev
(and the Baal HaGeulah of the 10th of Kislev)
in his maamar beginning with the words "Zeh"
[which apparently is the discourse "Atah Echad" that he said on the last Shabbos during his imprisonment
(Shabbos Parshas Vayeitzei,
the 9th of Kislev,
the year 5587)
before the Minchah prayer],
that in this entire formulation, the three lines of ChaGaT are explained four times,
in the four levels that encompass the entire order of Hishtalshelus,
beginning from before the Tzimtzum.
"You are One and Your Name is One, and who is like Your people Israel, one nation in the land" are the three lines of ChaGaT as they are before the Tzimtzum,
for even before the Tzimtzum there is the division of the three lines,
in a manner that the concept of division applies before the Tzimtzum.
"A crown of glory and a diadem of salvation, a day of rest and holiness You have given to Your people" is the matter of the three lines as they are after the Tzimtzum,
but in the worlds of Ein Sof that are above Atzilus and are not in a state of actual limitation
(as in Atzilus,
where there are vessels that limit),
and therefore it says about this "You have given to Your people,"
for "giving" means that it is given from hand to hand without change
(between before the Tzimtzum and after the Tzimtzum).
And after this
("Avraham will rejoice etc., rest of love and generosity etc.")
it speaks of the three lines as they are in Atzilus,
for in Atzilus they are in a state of limitation,
"ten and not nine, ten and not eleven."
And within this itself there are two levels,
"Avraham will rejoice, Yitzchak will sing, Yaakov and his sons will rest in it" refers to ChaGaT of Atzilus,
"rest of love and generosity, rest of truth and faith, rest of peace, tranquility and security" refers to NeHiY of Atzilus.
And as is explained at length in the aforementioned discourse.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section connects the four levels of the three lines to the four rungs of the ladder of prayer, based on the verse "And behold, a ladder set upon the earth" from Parshas Vayeitzei.

translations.translation: B)
And now, according to the known precision in the discourses of our Nesi'im,
that all the matters in them,
including also the time of their delivery,
are precise,
one should connect the aforementioned four levels with the verse
(in Parshas Vayeitzei,
for it can be said that this is one of the reasons that this maamar was said on Shabbos Parshas Vayeitzei)
"And behold, a ladder set upon the earth and its top reaches the heavens,"
which refers to the ladder of prayer,
"the ladder is prayer,"
that in the ladder of prayer there are four rungs.
For it can be said,
that the four rungs of prayer, in addition to the explanation that they correspond to the four worlds of ABiYA
(as explained in many places),
are in general corresponding to the aforementioned four levels,
the entirety of the order of Hishtalshelus,
beginning from before the Tzimtzum.
